    Morphisms between interval representations #

    Proposition 5.2 of the manuscript (Thomas): for interval representations M_{c,d} and M_{a,b} of the linearly oriented quiver, Hom(M_{c,d}, M_{a,b}) is one-dimensional if a ≤ c ≤ b ≤ d and zero otherwise, and a nonzero morphism has image M_{c,b}.

    A morphism η : M_{c,d} ⟶ M_{a,b} is determined by its coordinates coord η i ∈ k, the values at the unit vectors of the vertex spaces. The naturality squares give the equation coord_naturality, from which the vanishing conditions follow; when a ≤ c and b ≤ d every morphism is a scalar multiple of the canonical morphism canonicalHom, which factors as the projection M_{c,d} ⟶ M_{c,b} followed by the inclusion M_{c,b} ⟶ M_{a,b}.
